title: Anatomically precise and reversible control of osteogenesis

concept.text: The proposed innovation is selective, bidirectional control of bone formation: prevent unwanted bone from forming in soft tissues, biologically remove mature unwanted bone, and induce new bone within a chosen anatomical boundary where repair is needed. Heterotopic ossification is bone formation outside the normal skeleton. In fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), it progressively disables patients; the supplied review abstract also reports that surgical removal often leads to recurrence and expansion.

Conceptual synthesis: this capability requires control over location, timing and direction. Prevention must stop inappropriate osteogenesis; reversal must remove established heterotopic bone selectively; induction must build useful bone inside a prescribed volume and stop at its boundary. These are distinct biological functions. The proposed unifying advance is a shared control framework that can coordinate them, rather than an assumption that one molecular switch or one treatment will necessarily perform all three.

significance.text: FOP illustrates the clinical importance of this goal: progressive ossification of soft tissues causes severe disability, and recurrence after excision complicates removal. A safe biological means of preventing and reversing this process would address the complete-control goal identified in the supplied review abstract. Preventing additional lesions and removing established lesions would be separate benefits; slowing new bone formation alone would fulfill only part of the proposed capability.

Conditional impact synthesis: selectively removing bone that blocks a joint could improve movement in FOP and acquired heterotopic ossification, including cases associated with blast injury, neurological injury or hip surgery. Restored motion would depend on the remaining cartilage, muscles, tendons, nerves and joint architecture. Removing an obstruction cannot guarantee recovery when those structures are damaged, contracted or absent. Benefit in each acquired-HO setting would require clinical demonstration.

Conditional impact synthesis: anatomically confined induction could make bone reconstruction more controllable and potentially reduce unintended bone formation outside a repair site. Useful reconstruction would additionally require vascularization, integration with existing bone, appropriate mechanical strength and subsequent remodeling. Spatial confinement alone establishes none of these. Paired removal and induction would be a substantial orthopedic capability, but it would not itself regenerate a missing limb, restore a missing joint surface or demonstrate several-fold faster healing of ordinary fractures.

missing_breakthrough.text: The supplied FOP abstract identifies complete prevention, arrest and reversal of heterotopic ossification as unmet drug-treatment goals. Its statement concerns control of disease progression; it does not independently document a measured outcome in which functionally important mature heterotopic bone was resorbed. Selective removal of established bone is therefore a distinct requirement of this proposed innovation, beyond suppressing the formation of future lesions.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: the central selectivity problem is to distinguish unwanted bone and its precursors from the normal skeleton, healing fractures and developing growth plates. A reversal treatment would need to remove the intended mature lesion while preserving normal bone strength and avoiding injury to nearby nerves, vessels and soft tissues. Prevention would need to remain effective in the relevant disease or injury environment without broadly disabling necessary skeletal repair. These requirements make prevention and mature-bone resorption different therapeutic problems.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: the induction arm requires delivery and biological responses that respect a three-dimensional anatomical envelope over time. Treatment must support bone formation throughout the intended defect, avoid formation outside it, and terminate or become inactive once the required structure is established. Vascularization, load-bearing organization and remodeling are additional barriers. The research attributes loss of control partly to recombinant BMP-2 delivery, but the supplied review did not verify its specific diffusion, inflammation or burst-release assertions.

Scientific synthesis: shared involvement of bone-forming pathways does not establish that the same intervention can prevent lesions, resorb mature bone and induce a bounded repair. A common underlying control mechanism remains a hypothesis to demonstrate. Different agents or delivery systems might ultimately be required for each function; successful separate treatments would be valuable, while leaving the stronger claim of integrated bidirectional control to be tested.

current_state.text: The verified source is the abstract and metadata of the review by Yijun Zhou, Ce Shi and Hongchen Sun, published March 12, 2025, in Journal of Zhejiang University-SCIENCE B, volume 26, pages 317–332. It describes progressive, disabling heterotopic ossification in FOP, reports recurrence and expansion following surgical removal, and states that no definitive drug treatment completely prevents, halts or reverses HO progression in FOP. This is an attributed historical review assessment, not a demonstration of selective mature-bone removal or anatomically confined induction.

Access and timing limit that assessment. The retained source contains the abstract and article metadata, while the subscription preview omits the review body. Although published in March 2025, the article was accepted January 12, 2024. The supplied review includes no freshness assessment establishing coverage through November 1, 2026. Neither the historical abstract nor an uninspected related-article listing establishes whether the full paired capability remains unavailable at that later date.

The research reports that palovarotene is approved in the United States to reduce new heterotopic bone in FOP, and attributes modest radiographic benefit in post hoc analyses, premature growth-plate closure in children and no demonstrated disappearance of mature bone to articles dated November 19, 2024 (doi:10.1093/jbmrpl/ziae147), and January 21, 2025 (doi:10.1080/14656566.2025.2452938). No inspectable texts or source URLs for those articles were supplied. These approval, efficacy and safety assertions therefore remain unassessed in this record. No verified effect size or mature-bone resorption measurement can be given from the supplied evidence, and the evidence gap does not show that the reported findings are false.

The research also attributes to an August 8, 2025, acquired-HO review (doi:10.1186/s12891-025-09045-5) the position that established heterotopic bone is treated by surgical excision. That article's text was not supplied, so the breadth of this treatment claim, recurrence patterns and exceptions cannot be assessed here. The verified FOP abstract supports recurrence after surgery specifically in FOP; it does not establish management across ordinary acquired heterotopic ossification or how frequently surgery is avoided in FOP.

For the induction arm, the research cites Journal of Functional Biomaterials 16(9):313, dated August 29, 2025, for high-dose BMP-2 limitations involving burst release and ectopic bone. The source index contains its URL but no retained article artifact, so those assertions were not assessed in the supplied review. The broader claims that recombinant BMP-2 is approved, diffuses beyond the target and causes inflammatory complications likewise remain unverified here. The supplied material establishes neither a demonstrated paired control system nor its comprehensive present-day absence.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed prevention-and-reversal demonstration: in acquired ankylosing heterotopic ossification and separately in FOP, a drug or gene therapy would prevent new heterotopic bone and resorb functionally important mature lesions. Serial imaging would need to distinguish removal of established bone from reduced formation of new bone, and functional assessments would need to show whether removal produces useful motion. The proposal calls for motion to be maintained for two years. This duration is an author-proposed endpoint, not an established standard supported by the supplied sources.
completion_criteria.label: Prevent heterotopic ossification, resorb mature lesions, maintain two-year motion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safety boundaries: the treatment would preserve the normal skeleton without pathological fractures and, in pediatric use, avoid premature growth-plate closure. A convincing assessment would examine normal bone, ongoing repair and surrounding tissues as well as the treated lesion. Pediatric safety would require direct age-appropriate evidence; adult results could not establish it. Follow-up should also assess recurrence and the durability of functional improvement after treatment ends.
completion_criteria.label: Preserve normal bone without pathological fractures or premature growth-plate closure

completion_criteria.text: Proposed induction demonstration: in a human bone defect, treatment would generate bone confined to a predefined anatomical envelope on serial imaging. Assessment would measure both intended filling of the defect and any bone outside the boundary. Vascularization, integration, mechanical function and remodeling would require separate evidence if the result is claimed to be a useful living reconstruction. Anatomical confinement by itself would satisfy only the spatial-control component.
completion_criteria.label: Generate bone within predefined anatomical boundaries in human defects

completion_criteria.text: Proposed paired-control and reproducibility requirement: the two arms would demonstrate a shared underlying means of controlling osteogenesis, with its role in prevention, resorption and induction explicitly established. Either arm alone would be an important advance. Independent replication, defined treatment protocols and testing across relevant lesion locations, maturities, defect sizes and patient groups would establish the demonstrated breadth. Finite trials could not prove literal universality; the resulting claim should retain its tested anatomical, clinical, age and follow-up boundaries.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduce shared osteogenesis control within stated tested boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ORT-01, Adult epimorphic regeneration of a functional limb, would require coordinated regeneration of bone and many other tissues. ORT-08 could contribute control over where bone forms, but does not supply limb patterning or functional regeneration of the other structures. ORT-02, Biological restoration of the osteoarthritic synovial joint, concerns restoration of a joint as an integrated organ. Removing motion-blocking bone may help movement, but does not restore cartilage or the complete joint.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-04, Regeneration of the load-bearing tendon–bone enthesis, overlaps in the need to control mineralization at a precise tissue boundary. Its defining requirement is a functional force-transmitting tendon–bone interface. ORT-05, Restoration of the intervertebral disc as a living load-bearing organ, likewise depends on anatomical tissue organization, but disc restoration is not achieved by creating or removing bone.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-06, Force-bearing skeletal muscle after volumetric muscle loss, and ORT-07, Meaningful motor and sensory recovery across long peripheral-nerve gaps, address structures that may limit recovery even after obstructing heterotopic bone is removed. They could complement ORT-08 in complex injuries, while remaining distinct muscle and nerve regeneration problems.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-09, Regeneration of a functioning growth plate, overlaps with regulation of skeletal growth but requires restoration of an organized growth-producing structure. Preserving growth plates during ORT-08 treatment would be a safety requirement, not evidence that a lost growth plate has been regenerated. ORT-10, Single-episode restoration of segmental long bone by vascularized, remodelable bone, overlaps directly with the induction arm, but additionally requires repair of a substantial defect with vascularized, mechanically useful, remodelable tissue in a single treatment episode.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-03, Eradication of mature biofilm in bone and on orthopedic implants without removing the reconstruction, addresses infection control and preservation of an existing reconstruction. Precise osteogenesis could support subsequent repair, but neither selective bone resorption nor bounded bone induction establishes eradication of implant-associated biofilm. ORT-08 remains the distinct bidirectional-control concept within the roster.

change_log.change: Preserved ORT-08 and its title while separating prevention, mature-bone resorption and bounded induction.
change_log.reason: These are distinct functions; shared osteogenic biology does not demonstrate that one intervention can accomplish them all.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical present-day absence claim with a dated FOP review assessment and an explicit freshness limitation.
change_log.reason: A partial review accepted in January 2024 does not establish the complete state of the field through November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Corrected the missing-byline statement by naming Yijun Zhou, Ce Shi and Hongchen Sun.
change_log.reason: The supplied validated review identifies the authors in the retained article metadata.

change_log.change: Retained the palovarotene, acquired-HO and BMP-2 research assertions as specifically attributed, unassessed reports.
change_log.reason: Their inspectable source texts were absent. Preserving the reports with qualifications avoids treating missing evidence as disproof or silently discarding useful research detail.

change_log.change: Distinguished the abstract's reversal-of-progression statement from demonstrated resorption of mature heterotopic bone.
change_log.reason: The supplied abstract does not independently establish a measured mature-lesion removal outcome.

change_log.change: Made mobility benefits conditional and separated vascularization, mechanical function and remodeling from anatomical confinement.
change_log.reason: Removing obstructing bone does not repair all damaged joint structures, and spatially bounded formation does not establish a functional vascularized reconstruction.

change_log.change: Preserved the paired demonstration, two-year functional endpoint and pediatric safety requirements as proposals, and added explicit replication and scope boundaries.
change_log.reason: These are coherent operational goals, not source-established standards; finite testing establishes demonstrated breadth rather than universality.

change_log.change: Integrated distinctions for every other supplied roster entry without merging concepts.
change_log.reason: Bone control may contribute to regeneration and reconstruction, but does not itself fulfill the distinct tissue, organ or infection-control capabilities in those entries.

unresolved_issues: Whether any intervention had demonstrated the full paired capability by November 1, 2026 remains unresolved because the supplied material contains no adequate freshness assessment.

The supplied evidence does not establish selective biological resorption of functionally important mature heterotopic bone or show that a shared control mechanism can accomplish prevention, resorption and bounded induction.
Palovarotene approval details, effect sizes, post hoc analytical context, pediatric growth-plate outcomes and mature-lesion outcomes remain unassessed without the cited source texts.
The acquired-HO treatment claim and its scope, exceptions and recurrence outcomes remain unassessed without the cited review.
The BMP-2 approval, diffusion, inflammation, burst-release and ectopic-bone assertions remain unassessed because the cited article was not captured.
The full FOP review body was unavailable in the retained preview; its detailed evidence and qualifications cannot be inferred from the abstract.
The proposed two-year duration and anatomical-confinement criteria still need justified measurement methods, tolerances and clinically meaningful functional endpoints.

The review's recommendation to remove unverified palovarotene-specific and BMP-2 assertions was not adopted as deletion: they are retained as clearly attributed research reports with explicit evidence limitations, preserving useful detail without presenting them as established findings.

brief.title: Control over where bone grows and disappears
possible: People whose joints are blocked by unwanted bone could receive treatment that prevents further growth and biologically removes existing obstructions. People needing bone repair could grow new bone within a chosen boundary, with growth stopping where it should.

The goal is coordinated control over where bone forms, when it stops and where it is removed. Separate treatments might perform these jobs, but they would need to work within a shared control framework.
why: Bone growing in soft tissues can cause severe disability. Preventing it and removing existing growth could preserve or improve movement. Controlling the boundaries of new bone could also make reconstruction more predictable and reduce unwanted growth outside a repair site.

sources.who: Yijun Zhou, Ce Shi and Hongchen Sun
sources.showed: Their review describes disabling bone growth in soft tissues in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), a genetic disorder. It reports that surgical removal often leads to recurrence and expansion.
sources.quote: Despite surgical removal of HO, which often results in recurrence and expansion of ossification, there is currently no definitive drug treatment available to completely prevent, halt, or reverse the progression of HO in FOP.
sources.cited_for: FOP illustrates the need to prevent unwanted bone and remove established growth.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate selective removal of mature bone or repair confined to a chosen boundary.

sources.who: Authors of the Journal of Functional Biomaterials article
sources.showed: This article addresses rapid release and unwanted bone formation associated with high doses of a bone-growth protein.
sources.cited_for: It addresses delivery problems relevant to controlling where new bone forms.
sources.not_established: It does not establish coordinated prevention, removal and anatomically confined bone repair.

shown: Zhou and colleagues reviewed drug candidates for FOP. They described complete prevention, stopping and reversal of its unwanted bone growth as unmet treatment goals. Their review provides no demonstration of a treatment that selectively removes mature unwanted bone and also controls bounded repair.
missing: A treatment must prevent unwanted bone and remove established lesions while preserving useful movement.
Removal must spare normal bone, healing fractures and nearby tissues, including growing bones in children.
New bone must fill a chosen repair space, stay inside its boundary and stop growing when the structure is complete.
A shared means of controlling prevention, removal and repair must work reproducibly across clearly defined settings.

milestones.label: Prevention and removal with motion maintained for two years
milestones.explanation: Drug or gene therapy would have to prevent new growth, remove mature lesions and maintain motion for two years, separately in acquired joint-locking bone growth and FOP. This would establish prevention and reversal with lasting benefit.

milestones.label: Normal bone and childhood growth remain protected
milestones.explanation: Treatment would have to preserve normal bone without fractures from weakened bone or early closure of growth plates, where children's bones lengthen. This would establish that targeting unwanted bone spares necessary bone and growth.

milestones.label: New bone stays within a chosen human repair boundary
milestones.explanation: Repeated scans would have to show new bone filling a human bone defect while staying inside its predefined boundary. This would establish spatial control; blood supply, strength and integration would need separate evidence.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce shared control within tested limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce a shared means of controlling prevention, mature-bone removal and bounded repair across defined settings. This would establish coordinated control and the limits of its demonstrated reach.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether a shared biological control mechanism can coordinate prevention, mature-bone removal and bounded repair.
Removing a bone obstruction may not restore movement if the joint, muscles, tendons or nerves are already damaged.
The proposed two-year motion target and acceptable boundary tolerances still need clinically meaningful measurement criteria.

page.title: Spatial control of bone formation and resorption
page.definition: Treatments prevent heterotopic ossification—bone formation in soft tissues—remove established unwanted bone by cellular breakdown, and regenerate bone inside a specified repair volume while preserving the normal skeleton.

goal.need: FOP progressively restricts movement as bone accumulates in soft tissues. FDA compared 97 palovarotene-treated patients with 101 untreated patients; 39 participated in both studies. New bone still formed during treatment; FDA also reports growth-plate closure and increased radiographic vertebral fractures. Bone repair faces the converse problem: bone-inducing grafts can form bone outside the repair site.

figures.note: Weighted linear mixed-effect estimates from a nonrandomized external-control comparison. These measurements concern new bone formation.

completion.title: Clinical studies establish HO prevention, selective resorption and anatomically confined bone repair.
completion.criterion: For specified clinical indications, prospective controlled human studies demonstrate zero detected new heterotopic lesions during observation; net CT-measured resorption of baseline mature heterotopic bone without treatment-related loss of native bone; and union of a repair defect without detectable bone outside its prospectively defined repair volume. Imaging resolution, anatomical tolerance, follow-up and skeletal safety margins are specified in each protocol. Separate treatments may provide the three functions.
completion.set_by: Atlas; no outside body identified a combined prevention–resorption–repair acceptance test.
completion.basis: Searches of ICC guidance, FDA drug and bone-graft decisions, ClinicalTrials.gov FOP and spinal-fusion studies, ASTM osteoinduction guidance and bone-delivery papers found no combined clinical acceptance test. This Atlas criterion joins the published prevention/reversal and implant-confined regeneration goals. No universal follow-up, anatomical tolerance or native-bone safety margin was found.

milestones.title: A treatment bridges an 8-mm rat bone defect by 12 weeks while reducing bone outside a 6-mm envelope.
milestones.criterion: The published rat-defect test combines radiographic bridging of an 8-mm femoral gap by 12 weeks with reduced bone outside a 6-mm-diameter contour versus BMP-2 alone. On 3 January 2020, Hettiaratchi et al. reported bridging in 12/13 and 13/14 defects with two heparin-microparticle formulations. At 4 weeks, outside-envelope bone fractions were 39.4 ± 5.9% and 44.8 ± 7.9%, versus 65.8 ± 5.3% without microparticles. These are partial spatial restriction results.
milestones.set_by: Hettiaratchi et al., published rat-defect study protocol and Figure 5; an experiment-specific research test.
milestones.threshold_quote: bone volume was divided into defect volume and heterotopic volume based on 6-mm circular contours defined by the PCL nanofiber mesh.

milestones.title: Established heterotopic bone loses volume over 60 days in a rat model.
milestones.criterion: Longitudinal micro-CT demonstrates loss of previously established heterotopic bone over 60 days. Jin et al., published on 3 November 2021, reported this after engineered-osteoclast treatment in a rat tenotomy model, with 5 animals per group. A study published on 5 May 2026 also treated mouse HO after 7 weeks of formation: local VEGF-D reduced floating HO versus vehicle, with 5 mice per group; total HO volume did not differ significantly.
milestones.set_by: Jin et al., published animal-study protocol; the 60-day test is experiment-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: All rats were sacrificed 60 days after the initial injection

milestones.title: FDA authorizes a medicine that reduces new heterotopic ossification in FOP.
milestones.criterion: Marketing authorization covers reduction of new HO in a defined FOP population. Achieved on 16 August 2023 for palovarotene: females aged at least 8 years and males aged at least 10 years. FDA subsequently approved garetosmab on 19 August 2026 to reduce new HO lesions and clinician-assessed flare-ups in adults with FOP. These authorizations establish suppression of new lesions; neither indication claims removal of mature lesions.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, SOHONOS prescribing information and FOP marketing-authorization records.
milestones.threshold_quote: SOHONOS is indicated for the reduction in volume of new heterotopic ossification

milestones.title: A bone-inducing graft reduces 12-month failure after definitive closure of an open tibial fracture.
milestones.criterion: The FDA-reviewed INFUSE trial assesses failure within 12 months of definitive wound closure: further intervention recommended or performed to promote union, or screw breakage causing self-dynamization. FDA reports 38/149 failures with the 1.5 mg/mL bone morphogenetic protein-2 graft versus 66/150 controls, P=0.001. Approval followed on 30 April 2004. This endpoint contains no three-dimensional confinement criterion.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, INFUSE Bone Graft PMA P000054 Summary of Safety and Effectiveness Data, pivotal-study endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: secondary surgical intervention to promote fracture healing within 12 months

milestones.title: Biological treatment shrinks mature heterotopic bone in people while preserving native bone.
milestones.criterion: Baseline mature HO loses mineralized volume on serial CT after biological treatment, with native-bone preservation demonstrated against prospectively specified skeletal safety margins. LUMINA-1 randomized 44 adults with FOP: 20 to garetosmab and 24 to placebo. Its post hoc pre-existing-lesion analysis found a 28-week difference in time-weighted percentage volume change of −4.8 percentage points versus placebo, with a 95% confidence interval of −23.6 to 14.1. That result does not establish mature-lesion reversal.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches of ICC guidance and registered FOP protocols found no clinical acceptance threshold combining mature-lesion resorption with preservation of native bone.

milestones.title: Bone bridges a human repair defect without detectable growth outside its planned volume.
milestones.criterion: A human repair defect achieves union, with no new bone detectable outside its prospectively specified repair volume on serial CT. Imaging resolution, permitted anatomical tolerance and follow-up are protocol-specific. CMS lists the OsteoAdapt SP IDE study G230350/NCT07627997 with approval on 30 September 2026; that coverage decision supplies no result for this spatial endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Atlas, operationalizing Theradaptive's published implant-localization goal; searches of FDA graft reviews, ASTM guidance and spinal-fusion trial records found no clinical anatomical tolerance.

not_found: No external acceptance test for the combined prevention, selective resorption and bounded-repair capability was found.
No registered clinical acceptance threshold coupling mature-HO shrinkage to preservation of native skeletal bone was found.
No externally specified clinical tolerance for bone outside a prescribed repair volume was found.
The cited Springer page exposed the Zhou review's abstract, but not its full text.
The full ClinicalTrials.gov record for NCT07627997 could not be read; its CMS IDE listing was accessible.
